The flow speed in the second section is given by \( v = Q/A \), where \( Q = 9.5 \, \text{L/s} = 0.0095 \, \text{m}^3/\text{s} \) and \( A = \pi (0.02 \, \text{m})^2 = 0.0004\pi \, \text{m}^2 \). Thus \( v = 0.0095/(0.0004\pi) = 23.75/\pi \approx 7.56 \, \text{m/s} \).

The centripetal acceleration is \( a = v^2/r \) with \( v = 2\pi r/T \). Given \( r = 5.0 \, \text{m} \) and \( T = 4.0 \, \text{s} \), \( a = 4\pi^2 r/T^2 = 5\pi^2/4 \approx 12.3 \, \text{m/s}^2 \).

The gravitational force is \( F = G M m / r^2 \). Using \( G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N·m}^2/\text{kg}^2 \), \( M = 0.500 \, \text{kg} \), \( m = 0.0100 \, \text{kg} \), \( r = 0.0500 \, \text{m} \), we get \( F = 1.33 \times 10^{-10} \, \text{N} \), so \( X = 1.33 \).

From Kepler’s third law, \( a = a_{\text{Earth}} (T/T_{\text{Earth}})^{2/3} \). With \( a_{\text{Earth}} = 1.496 \times 10^{11} \, \text{m} \) and \( T = 4.62 \, \text{years} \), \( a = 1.496 \times 10^{11} \times (4.62)^{2/3} \approx 4.15 \times 10^{11} \, \text{m} \).

ANSWER: 7.56,12.3,1.33,4.15
